newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas pares losses late but still down.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas pares losses late but still down.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by some late short covering, pared losses Thursday in moderate activity, but an unexpectedly-bearish AGA report Wednesday still kept the complex on the defensive.
At 1430 EST, February was 5.3 cents lower at $3.46 per million British thermal units, while March was down by 11.6 cents at $3.06. Most others were down by 0.4 to 6.3 cents.

"Are these (futures) values justified versus the growing storage surplus? If we didn't have a cold front in place, we'd probably be trading in the $2.50s," said one Houston trader, noting Gulf cash plunged to that level early this month.

AGA said U.S. gas stocks fell last week by just 15 bcf, well-below average expectations in the 70-85 bcf range. Stocks are now 69 bcf above year-ago levels, the first time in more than a year that overall U.S. gas inventories are in surplus to year-ago. And eastern storage stands 211 bcf, or almost 20 percent, above last year.
While colder weather forecasts for this week and next tempered the bears, few expected much upside, with the surplus in storage likely to grow even more comfortable near-term.

Technically, traders still pegged February support in the remaining gap between $3.11 and $3.25, with better buying likely in the $2.60s. Resistance was seen at $3.57 and then in the $3.80-3.84 area and at $3.96. The contract high is $4.02.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped Thursday by 15-20 cents to the $3.60 area. Midcontinent pipes were down about a nickel to the low-$3.80s. New York city gate gas was talked on either side of $4.00, off about 30 cents on the day.
NYMEX said 26,762 Hub contracts traded at 1400 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1430 EST.
On the KCBT, February fell five cents to $3.28, while deferreds were three to 15 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.3 cent to 18.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
